title: Tamsin and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of a collapsing republic, courier Astrid Nystrom carries diplomatic codes to a neutral port, believing herself a bystander to history. At her boarding house door she finds a child named Tamsin, left with a note instructing her to forget the face — and discovers the girl is the daughter of General Veyra, the republic's newly declared enemy, whom Astrid secretly promised years ago in peacetime that no child of hers would ever be taken. Hunted by both sides, Astrid must choose between delivering her codes and keeping her promise, learning that invisibility was always an illusion. The story ends with Astrid burning the ledger that lists Tamsin among 'assets to be recovered,' smuggling the girl across the border at terrible personal cost, and accepting that identity is not what history assigns you but what you refuse to surrender.
about_author: Astrid Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records from forgotten border wars. She writes historical fiction about the people paperwork tried to erase.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the capital's final chaotic weeks, she receives her courier commission and sews the code-cylinder into her coat lining. She tells herself she is furniture, not history. Emotional beat: anxious denial, the comfort of being unimportant.

chapters.title: Departure on the Grey Coach
chapters.summary: Astrid travels north with three other passengers, including a nervous ministry clerk who talks too much. She memorizes faces out of habit. Beat: wary observation; the republic's decay seen through coach windows.

chapters.title: The Boarding House at Marrow Quay
chapters.summary: Astrid arrives at the fog-bound port town and settles into Mrs. Halloway's boarding house, awaiting the ship that will carry her codes onward. Beat: uneasy stillness before the storm.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A knock at dawn reveals six-year-old Tamsin, frozen and silent, with a note: forget the face. Astrid recognizes the handwriting as General Veyra's from years ago. Beat: shock and dread.

chapters.title: What Was Promised in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: young Astrid, then a clerk, met Veyra during treaty negotiations and made a careless promise over a child's cradle. Beat: guilt surfacing; promises have longer lives than treaties.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: The ministry clerk recognizes Tamsin's name from a confiscated ledger listing enemy children as assets to be recovered. He leaves to report it. Beat: the machinery of power turns its attention toward them.

chapters.title: Mrs. Halloway's Silence
chapters.summary: Mrs. Halloway's POV. The landlady chooses not to see the child, revealing her own history of lost daughters. Beat: complicity and quiet solidarity between women who survive by looking away.

chapters.title: Soldiers at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Republic troops occupy Marrow Quay; ships are seized, curfew imposed. Astrid realizes her diplomatic passage is now worthless. Beat: claustrophobia; escape routes closing one by one.

chapters.title: Teaching a Child to Be Invisible
chapters.summary: Astrid coaches Tamsin in silence, disguise, and stillness — the skills of her own trade turned to survival. Beat: tenderness hardening into strategy; motherhood as tradecraft.

chapters.title: The Clerk Returns
chapters.summary: The clerk returns with soldiers' pay and a bargain: hand over the girl, keep your career. Astrid refuses for the first time aloud. Beat: the point of no return; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Burning the First Page
chapters.summary: Astrid steals a copy of the ledger and burns Tamsin's page, erasing her from the record. Beat: defiant hope; paper can be fought with fire.

chapters.title: Veyra's Letter
chapters.summary: A hidden second note in Tamsin's coat reveals Veyra knew the cost and chose Astrid deliberately — trust across enemy lines. Beat: the weight of being trusted by someone history calls a monster.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Astrid bargains with a harbor smuggler, paying with her code-cylinder — betraying her mission to save her charge. Beat: sacrifice; the courier becomes a traitor to her own side.

chapters.title: Interrogation at the Customhouse
chapters.summary: Astrid is detained and questioned by an officer who suspects everything and proves nothing. She lies fluently for the first time. Beat: terror mastered; the invisible woman learns to be seen wrongly.

chapters.title: Tamsin Alone
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Left hiding in a coal cellar, the child ventures out to find Astrid and nearly betrays them both. Beat: fear through small eyes; love outrunning caution.

chapters.title: The Officer's Doubt
chapters.summary: The interrogating officer finds the burned ledger fragment and hesitates — his own niece is listed too. He delays the search order. Beat: corruption cracking from within; even enforcers have faces they protect.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: Astrid and Tamsin flee through frozen marshland toward the smuggler's boat, pursued by dogs and lanterns. Beat: relentless rising action; cold, exhaustion, and resolve.

chapters.title: The River Ice
chapters.summary: Climax begins: the crossing fails; the smuggler is captured; Astrid must carry Tamsin across breaking river ice as searchlights sweep. Beat: peak physical peril.

chapters.title: Face to Face with Veyra
chapters.summary: On the far bank, Veyra himself waits — stripped of rank, hunted too. Astrid confronts the general whose promise she kept and whose war orphaned her mission. Beat: emotional climax; judgment, gratitude, and grief entwined.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: Veyra offers Astrid sanctuary under a new name in exile. Astrid realizes she cannot vanish again — she has become someone. Beat: identity claimed; invisibility renounced.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: News arrives that the republic has fallen and the ledger survived in other hands; the hunt continues beyond borders. Astrid and Veyra part ways to draw pursuit apart. Beat: bittersweet resolution; victory without safety.

chapters.title: Tamsin and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Years later, Astrid — living openly under her own name — watches grown Tamsin burn the last surviving copy of the ledger herself. Beat: resolution and theme fulfilled; justice outside the law, passed to the next generation.
